transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-03
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Greene (Redwood SE), Noah Kim (Redwood CSM), Jia Li (Redwood Legal Ops); Lena Ortiz, Dr. Aaron Chu, Priya Das, Marko Velen (Solace)

Summary (auto): Quick procurement touch to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, KMS/encryption, pilot pricing, and onboarding timeline. Action items assigned for redline, SOC2 docs, and pilot tenant provisioning.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we can do intros quick, i'm maya patel redwood... um account executive - ethan's gonna run the technical parts.
[00:12] Lena: Hi maya, lena here - thanks. priya will handle procurement, marko is on for security, and aaron is joining from AI.
[00:20] Ethan: Hey all, quick agenda - MSA/DPA items, SLAs, KMS/encryption, pilot pricing and onboarding checklist. we'll pause for Qs. sound good?
[00:30] Priya: yep that works.
[01:05] Marko: real quick - key thing for us is audit logs and encryption keys uptime SLA, we use internal HSM and want to see how redwood integrates with our KMS.
[01:40] Ethan: absolutely - we support customer-managed KMS via standard KMIP and have integrations for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM. there is a small note in the DPA about key escrow and access patterns, which we can clarify.
[02:15] Maya: on the MSA we've marked up three main asks from your counsel: data residency clause, deletion/return clause, and liability caps. we can walk through each.
[02:50] Dr. Aaron: circling back on data residency - our models will handle PHI-ish medical notes in pilot, need to confirm whether the hosted offering keeps data in region or requires private deployment.
[03:20] Maya: good call - so for pilot we usually start hosted with a regional tenancy; if you need VPC/private deployment we can move to Redwood Private but that adds timeline and costs.
[03:55] Priya: procurement wants clear SLAs tied to uptime and RTO for incidents - what's standard?
[04:20] Ethan: for hosted we publish a 99.9% uptime SLA on the dedicated plan, and have escalation path. for Private we can negotiate higher SLAs. also we do per-token latency targets in the console if we agree on model/instance sizing.
[04:50] Marko: latency targets are fine, but availability during batch processing is a concern because we run high volume nightly jobs. how does batching affect SLA?
[05:15] Ethan: batching is client-configurable - our runtime does continuous batching to optimize cost, but it respects per-request latency SLOs when configured. we can propose a profile for your nightly throughput that keeps availability guaranteed.
[05:45] Lena: can you send a sample configuration and cost delta between low-latency and batch-optimized profiles?
[06:05] Maya: yes we'll include that in pricing - sample config + delta numbers.
[06:30] Priya: on the DPA, there are a few redlines around subprocessor lists and audit rights, legal wants either list or 30-day notice before adding.
[06:55] Jia Li: (Redwood legal) we can accept notice and an option for a vendor list in a schedule; can't always promise fixed vendor list but we do a 30-day notice + audit support.
[07:25] Priya: ok that's helpful. also question around data deletion - they want physical destruction guarantee for any cached data.
[07:45] Ethan: our runtime uses KV cache for prefixes - we can guarantee logical deletion and immediate eviction from cache; physical destruction on underlying infra depends on provider but we provide attestations. for on-prem/private we can provide more control.
[08:10] Dr. Aaron: do you have SOC 2 Type II and penetration test reports we can share?
[08:25] Ethan: yes, SOC 2 Type II and recent pentest summary. i'll attach the reports - note some redactions.
[08:40] Marko: and encryption at rest - are keys ever handled by redwood?
[08:55] Ethan: not unless you opt into managed KMS. default we use server-side encryption managed by cloud provider; with customer-managed KMS your keys never leave your control.
[09:20] Lena: good. on pricing, procurement asked for a pilot rate and a committed monthly cap - can you propose a pilot SKU?
[09:45] Maya: we usually do a 30-day pilot with reserved capacity window and a discounted pilot rate. i'll put together a two-tier proposal: pilot discounted per-token with a cap, then month-to-month for scale.
[10:10] Priya: procurement needs that proposal in writing for approvals.
[10:20] Maya: we'll send the pilot proposal and T&Cs.
[10:35] Dr. Aaron: technical Q - model variants and rollbacks: if you route to smaller quantized variants for cost, does that change outputs unpredictably?
[11:00] Ethan: we provide model profiles with quality-impact notes; in our routing policy we expose canary and A/B rollout controls and automatic fallback. we'll share eval metrics comparing model variants so you can approve any fallback.
[11:35] Lena: please include those evals.
[11:45] Maya: noted.
[12:10] Marko: about audit logs - retention period options? legal wants 3 years.
[12:35] Jia Li: we can offer tiered retention; default is 90 days in hosted, extended retention is available as an add-on up to multi-year with export support. we'll propose options in the DPA schedule.
[13:00] Priya: any additional compliance like ISO?
[13:15] Ethan: we have SOC 2 Type II currently; ISO 27001 is in roadmap but not certified yet.
[13:35] Dr. Aaron: for pilot we can accept SOC 2 only.
[13:45] Maya: ok.
[14:10] Priya: SLAs for data breach notifications - what's your timeline?
[14:30] Jia Li: we commit to 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches; we can add contractual language in MSA.
[14:50] Marko: liability cap - client side counsel wants lower cap than standard, around 2x fees for gross negligence carveouts; is that feasible?
[15:10] Maya: typical redwood cap is 1x annual fees but for enterprise we can negotiate higher in exchange for increased fees. we'll surface options.
[15:40] Priya: procurement will need that in writing with cost tradeoffs.
[16:00] Ethan: separate technical note: for VPC/private deployments we need about 4-6 weeks to stand up the environment plus validation. if you want pilot in 2 weeks, we'd do hosted regional tenancy.
[16:30] Lena: timeline is aggressive - initial business sign-off wanted by 3/15. is hosted acceptable to legal?
[16:50] Jia Li: hosted in-region with SOC2 + DPA redlines should be acceptable for pilot; private could follow once procurement approves longer timeline and budget.
[17:15] Dr. Aaron: any network egress/data residency flags we should be aware of for EU data?
[17:40] Ethan: we can pin region to EU, and if required we can do private deployment in EU region. region pinning is in the control plane.
[18:00] Priya: procurement needs pricing broken down (pilot, production, private infra uplift, SLA premium).
[18:20] Maya: we'll provide a pricing spreadsheet with line items.
[18:45] Lena: thanks.
[19:05] Maya: quick note on contract workflow - we'll send a redline and ask for counter from your counsel, then legal-to-legal review. our legal ops (jia) will own the redline.
[19:35] Jia Li: yes i'll track redline and provide comments.
[20:00] Priya: are there any subprocessor concerns with third-party inference infra?
[20:20] Ethan: we list major cloud providers; for dedicated environments we can restrict subprocessors and provide 30-day notice before changes.
[20:45] Marko: pentest scope - can we do a shared pentest of the integration?
[21:05] Ethan: we support a scoping call; typically we provide a pentest summary and allow customer scoping with a white-listing window. full co-penetration needs SOW but doable.
[21:35] Dr. Aaron: regarding model outputs, we need SLA on nondeterministic variance for exact classification outputs used in downstream triage - any guarantees?
[21:55] Ethan: we don't guarantee deterministic outputs but we can provide evaluation thresholds on precision/recall for your test prompts and put regression alerts. we'll include eval harness results.
[22:25] Lena: please include the eval harness + sample prompts.
[22:40] Noah: i'll provision the pilot tenant and shared workspace, you'll get access to the console and metrics.
[23:00] Priya: onboarding checklist?
[23:10] Noah: yes - we'll include API keys, SSO config (SAML), role-based access, and test prompt set ingestion.
[23:35] Marko: SSO - does Redwood support SCIM for provisioning?
[23:50] Ethan: yes SCIM + SAML SSO are supported; we'll share setup docs.
[24:10] Priya: great.
[24:40] Maya: pricing note - if you commit to 12-month reserved capacity we can lower the unit price by ~25% vs on-demand. pilot won't lock you in.
[25:05] Priya: procurement will consider reserved discount but need forecasting accuracy.
[25:30] Lena: question on support - is there a named CSM for pilot?
[25:45] Noah: yes i'll be primary CSM and support triage with our eng team.
[26:05] Dr. Aaron: telemetry - can we get token-level traces for debugging?
[26:25] Ethan: yes token-level trace is available in the console for authorized roles; we can redact sensitive data fields.
[26:45] Marko: are there tags for data classification in logs?
[27:00] Ethan: yes you can tag and we support PII masking patterns.
[27:25] Priya: procurement requires insurance certificates - does Redwood carry cyber liability?
[27:45] Maya: yes we carry cyber liability and can share certs.
[28:05] Priya: good.
[28:30] Maya: ok let me summarize real quick - next steps: 1) maya to send redline and pilot pricing, 2) ethan to share SOC2 + KMS details and evals, 3) noah to provision pilot tenant and onboarding doc, 4) priya to confirm procurement timeline and approvers.
[29:00] Priya: yep.
[29:20] Dr. Aaron: tech follow-up - can you include sample latency percentiles for the model variant we discussed?
[29:45] Ethan: yes p50/p90/p99 figures and cost per 1k tokens for the variant.
[30:05] Lena: any questions from redwood side about internal approvers?
[30:20] Priya: procurement approvers are listed as: CFO (final), Head of Security (technical sign-off), Legal counsel (contract). i'll send names.
[30:40] Maya: perfect, we'll align timelines.
[31:00] Marko: one more security note - we need MFA enforced for console access.
[31:15] Noah: MFA is available and enforceable via SSO.
[31:30] Priya: can we get a timeline for when Redwood Dedicated could be deployed if approved?
[31:50] Ethan: Redwood Dedicated (dedicated pools) typically 6-8 weeks; private on-prem longer. for EU region it can be slightly longer due to capacity.
[32:10] Lena: we will likely do hosted pilot then Dedicated for production.
[32:30] Maya: sounds good.
[33:00] Priya: any gotchas on export controls or export of data to US?
[33:20] Jia Li: we'll include data residency language; we can commit to region pinning and export restrictions as needed with addendum.
[33:45] Marko: last thing - SLA credits mechanism in case of breach?
[34:00] Jia Li: typical SLA credits formula is available in MSA; we can negotiate specific credit percentages for tier.
[34:25] Priya: procurement will push for larger credits.
[34:45] Maya: noted.
[35:10] Dr. Aaron: is there an NDA or separate DPA we need to sign first?
[35:25] Maya: the DPA will be an exhibit to MSA; we can do a mutual NDA if you prefer before exchanging docs.
[35:40] Priya: we have an NDA already with a partner; i'll check.
[35:55] Maya: ok.
[36:20] Ethan: i'll also share a short technical SOW for the pilot - integration steps and acceptance criteria.
[36:40] Lena: good.
[37:05] Priya: procurement window - we target approvals by 3/15, so redline and pricing need to be steady by 3/8.
[37:25] Maya: we'll aim for 3/5 redline and 3/8 pricing final.
[37:45] Noah: i'll start provisioning once redline accepted.
[38:10] Dr. Aaron: one more question - does Redwood keep model logs or input retention for debugging?
[38:30] Ethan: we keep minimal request logs by default; full request/response retention is opt-in and covered in DPA. we can do ephemeral mode for sensitive content.
[38:55] Marko: can we get a diagram of network flow and where logs are stored?
[39:10] Ethan: yes i'll attach network diagram.
[39:35] Priya: ok thanks.
[39:50] Maya: any blockers?
[40:05] Priya: none immediate, just need documented items.
[40:25] Maya: great.
[40:40] Ethan: we'll follow up with attachments.
[41:00] Maya: thanks everyone - recap: redline by 3/5, SOC2 & KMS + network diagrams by 3/4, pricing by 3/8, pilot tenant by 3/6. schedule legal review around 3/10.
[41:25] Priya: yes we'll schedule.
[41:40] Dr. Aaron: thanks, appreciate it.
[41:55] Lena: thanks.
[42:10] Noah: talk soon.
[42:25] Maya: end call.
